dog.description_text:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Cardinal was surrendered to the care center as a stray, and we have no history on his behavior in a home environment. The person who found Cardinal reported that he was gentle, easygoing, and calm for the day that they had him; however, he has not acclimated well to the care center environment, and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. He has shown fearful behavior on being removed from his kennel, escalating to hard barking, growling, and baring teeth. While on walks, he has remained tense and tail tucked. Due to his level of fear, we recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can allow for decompression, provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based), and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes: Cardinal â™¥ï¸ If you spend even a few minutes in the shelter, you can understand why so many dogs, including Cardinal, are scared. To add to that, he was found alone in a park with no collar or leash or owner in sight. His finder spent a day with him looking for his home, and when they couldn't they brought him to the shelter. They said he was gentle and easy going and the intake staff agreed.

And so did we. In spite of his intense initial fear, his reluctance to be handled or assessed, the gentle boy was there when we met him. His little pout and those gorgeous eyes looking up at us show a lost young boy trying to make sense of where he is and who all these new people are. He climbs onto my lap for cuddles while I know he was the same dog who was too scared to have a collar put on him when he arrived. I imagine with more gentleness and stability, the real Cardinal will come out to meet the person who is lucky enough to call him theirs.
dog.name: Cardinal
